# Northwind Telecom — eSIM setup

*Synthetic document. Northwind Telecom is a fictional operator invented for testing; every figure
below is made up and describes no real product, tariff or person.*

## What you need

A handset that supports eSIM, a working internet connection on that handset, and the QR code sent to
the email address on the account. The QR code is valid for 7 days and can be used once.

## Installing the profile

Open the handset's mobile-network settings, choose to add a data plan, and scan the QR code. The
profile downloads in under a minute on a normal connection. Do not delete the profile once it is
installed; a deleted profile cannot be reinstalled from the same QR code.

## Converting a physical SIM to eSIM

Request the conversion from the app. The physical SIM keeps working until the eSIM profile is
activated, and stops within an hour afterwards. Conversion is free once every 90 days; a second
conversion inside that window costs ₹100.

## Changing handsets

An eSIM profile does not move by itself. Request a fresh QR code from the app before you stop using
the old handset, because the request needs a signed-in session on the account. A fresh QR code is
free once every 30 days.

## Using eSIM and a physical SIM together

A dual-SIM handset can run the Northwind eSIM alongside another operator's physical SIM. Set which
SIM carries data in the handset's settings; the setting does not change anything on the network
side.

## If the QR code will not scan

Check that the code has not already been used, that it is less than 7 days old, and that the
handset is online. A profile can also be installed by entering the activation code printed under
the QR code by hand.

## Handsets that are not supported

A handset locked to another operator cannot install the profile even if it supports eSIM. A handset
bought outside India may support eSIM without supporting the bands used here; the profile installs
but the connection stays on 4G.
